objective: Take up LOOP-NET-20261108-001's direction 1, relayed by the coordinator on 2026-11-08 (G5 with G1): on the square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced contacts, find which contacts each contact needs and at which lags, then test whether a ring of cuts separates the torus; stop at a theorem or at the size where composition stops reaching. status: Complete 2026-11-08: proved that on the n x n square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced contacts influence spreads by the powers of L = x + 1/x + y + 1/y over GF(2), so a contact needs a ring exactly when an odd number of walks lead from it, first at lag g k + 1 and then at recurring lags; on odd tori every contact needs every ring, on even tori no contact ever needs the antipodal ring (finite feedback at powers of two); cutting the contacts round any set of rings separates it (native separation on odd tori), one ring of cuts round the torus does not separate and two do. Recommendation Research directions (genus read by rings of cuts, or which lattices compose everywhere).
stop_rule: Stop at a theorem for the square lattice, or at the torus size where composition stops reaching.
